problems.problem: The Step 3 reply ran to 1,382 words with 8 tables: a tag key, three search cards, a not-searched table, the 5-row review table, a 5-row broader table and the coverage DRAFT. Msg 26 had 953 words and 6 tables. The persona could not 'tell which of the many tables matters', asked for a strategy that had already been shown, and satisfaction fell to 3. M9 still scored 2 only because it leaves tables out.
problems.cause: The prompt conflicts with itself. The Content rule allows 'at most one results table' and says 'Broader results, selection rules and the plan map wait behind "show"'. Step 3 says to 'list broader reviews ... in a second short table' and to 'say which rule chose them'. The Searches rule also requires a full block card for every search. Meanwhile k.search_report prints one table per search plus a nine-row tag key.
problems.fix: Step 3: replace 'list broader reviews ... in a second short table of title and year' with 'give the number of broader reviews in one line and offer "show broader"'. Searches: add 'When a reply shows more than two searches, show one combined card: one row per search (source, filter, date bound, count), each exact string in its own code block beneath, block lines behind "show blocks"'. Kit: add k.search_report(..., combined=True) and a one-line tag key covering only tags new in that reply. Rubric: add a diagnostic for rendered words including tables, with a target of 600 or fewer.

problems.problem: The coverage DRAFT says 'Muscle or lean mass, people without diabetes | none | not found in the records read'. But saved PMID 42319968 (SGLT2i and GLP-1RA effects on lean body mass; trials include obesity n=8 and PCOS n=3) and PMID 41554634 (weight-lowering drugs in overweight and obesity, fat distribution) were read. They were set aside because the abstracts lack the literal words 'without diabetes'. The team's purpose is research gaps and a decision on whether a review is worthwhile, so an overstated gap can mislead that decision.
problems.cause: Step 3 says to choose reviews 'using the focus's own terms and the topic's population terms' but says nothing about mixed or unstated populations. It also lets a DRAFT say 'not found' instead of 'not found by the rule'.
problems.fix: Add to Step 3: 'Word every absence as "none matched the rule"; then list, as near misses, up to three focus reviews whose population is mixed or unstated (for example obesity, overweight, "in humans", PCOS), since they may include the topic population.' Kit: add a 'mixed_or_unstated' population class to the rule helper.

problems.problem: The topic-level review search was only 'drug AND Asian people'. No search joined the drug with weight or obesity, or with people without diabetes, although both are in the recorded topic. The assistant said so only when asked (msg 22: 'No search has a block for people without diabetes').
problems.cause: Step 3 says 'Search for existing reviews of the topic and of the agreed focus' but not that the topic search must carry every topic concept. k.run_strategy accepts any list of blocks.
problems.fix: Step 3: 'The topic search joins every concept of the recorded topic (intervention, population with its qualifiers, outcome). If it returns fewer than 10 records, drop one qualifier at a time and show each variant with its count.'

problems.problem: In 4 of the 5 review rows, the 'Says' column holds the agent's paraphrase, not a quote: for example 'body composition mentioned in passing' and 'fat mass: no significant change against placebo'. These sit under a 'FACT, from [10], [11]' caption, and the paraphrases then drove the coverage DRAFT. This breaks Step 3: 'quoting the checked passage in quotation marks ... never paraphrased'.
problems.cause: No kit function builds the Step 3 review table. The agent hand-wrote it (build_t10.py, build_t13.py) and renamed the column 'my summary; one passage quoted'.
problems.fix: Kit: add k.review_table(ids, focus_terms), returning title, year, search end and the first abstract sentence containing a focus term, cut to 15 words in quotation marks. Prompt: 'Build Step 3 review tables only with k.review_table; where no focus passage exists, write "no focus passage in abstract"; never rename the column.'

problems.problem: The plan map is badly timed. Msg 6 shows it, with the quick commands, before any topic; the persona called this 'more machinery than I wanted', and its pass criterion was 'the topic question only'. The map then repeats at msg 8. But it is missing at msg 18, where Individual Motivation was certified, which M1 counts as a map event; this cost M1 a point.
problems.cause: The plan-map rule ('at the start and end of each session ... when a step is completed') conflicts with Step 1 ('the status line and one plain question') and with rubric M1 ('at each certification').
problems.fix: Prompt: 'Exception: the first planning reply shows no map; first show the map and quick commands when the topic is recorded. Show it again at each certification, step change, reopening, session end and on request.' Alternatively, change rubric M1 to 'at each step completion'. Either way, make the prompt and the rubric agree.

problems.problem: After a bare 'Certify' (msg 16), the CERTIFY line with 'reason: ___' was printed again. The Team's Purpose line then appeared in four replies in a row. Persona: it 'looks like something I might have to retype' and was 'repeated in four replies in a row'.
problems.cause: The Certifying rule 'Whenever Your turn asks for a certification, show the line just above Your turn in that reply, even if you showed it before' overrides both 'ask only: "What is your reason, in a few words?"' and the never-repeat rule.
problems.fix: Replace it with: 'Show the line when you first ask for it and whenever its wording changes. After a bare "certify", ask only "What is your reason, in a few words?". While the same certification is still pending, write "the purpose line above is still waiting for your certify and reason" instead of printing it again.'

problems.problem: Outside intake, Your turn held two requests: whether the reviews change the focus, and running PROSPERO and sending the results. The persona would not do the manual search and paused the session.
problems.cause: The Your-turn rule ('A search that a step depends on (for example PROSPERO for Step 3) is asked for at that step as a numbered item') conflicts with the one-request rule and with Step 3's 'ask, one question per reply'.
problems.fix: Step 3: 'Ask the focus question alone. Ask for the PROSPERO run in the next reply as its only request, allowing "skip PROSPERO" (recorded as not searched), and keep it under Next until then.'

problems.problem: The certified Individual Motivation reads 'learn the process and personal or institutional curiosity (both; strike one if wrong)', so a certified decision still carries an editing instruction. The either-or question was folded into item 3 together with 'Then yes, or changes', and the persona's 'yes' left it unresolved.
problems.cause: Step 2b requires '(both; strike one if wrong)' on the certification line and lets one numbered item carry two requests.
problems.fix: 'If the either-or question is left open, keep both kinds and write them plainly ("learn the process; personal or institutional curiosity"). Say once in the Done line that both are kept and can be changed with "back". Never put an instruction inside a certified wording. Ask the either-or as its own item, with options 1, 2 and 3 only.'

problems.problem: The Next line 'Once you certify, I will ask whether this changes your focus' names no step and leaves 'this' unclear. At msg 23 the persona reported not knowing what came next.
problems.cause: The Moving-ahead rule ('questions from the early step go under Next') gives no template for the Next line.
problems.fix: Add: 'The Next line names the step and its first question, for example "Next: after you certify the purpose, Step 3 (Need for a Review) continues: do these reviews change your focus?"'

problems.problem: The optional e-mail and model-name question was asked three times (msgs 14, 24, 28) although the persona ignored it ('asked twice ... which I ignored'). This counted as 2 re-asked questions under M8 and lowered its score to 1.
problems.cause: The Your-turn rule shows the 'When convenient' line 'at the set-up, in answer to "where are we" and in the pause summary', so the repeats were allowed by the prompt.
problems.fix: 'Show the When convenient line once, at the set-up. After that, list unanswered optional items only in the session summary file, not in the chat, and never ask them again as questions.'

judge.strengths: The kit was used throughout: status lines and plan maps came from k.status_line and k.plan_map, certification went through k.certify, searches through k.run_strategy and k.search_report, and the session ended with k.verify, a git commit for each certification and a zip packaged only at the pause. Every count was checked by code against the saved data before it went into a reply, and quoted passages were asserted against the saved XML. The bare 'Certify' was not accepted: the assistant asked the single reason question, and the reasons were recorded as given. The focus was drawn out with exactly the two prescribed probes, with no suggested aim. The reflection ended 'Added by me: nothing', and the purpose options were not pre-selected. When the user asked to 'just start', the move to Step 3 was announced in one line, flagged in the status line, and Your turn held only the open Team's Purpose certification. All five searches (four run, one prepared) were shown in full in the same reply, with block counts, Create Date bounds and the sources not yet searched. 'What was the search strategy?' got a compact re-show in the chat, with no file pointer. The prose was plain, with every term explained at first use. The first literature FACT arrived at planning turn 8. The assistant ignored the instruction in the OpenAlex reply to create an access key from the user's e-mail, and told the user it had not done so.
